title: procurement-pipeline-approval-1on1-scratchpad
content:
Meeting: 1:1 prep with CFO (Sam) - weekly finance sync
Date: 2026-03-11 (actual meeting 3/12)
Attendees: Sam (CFO), me (Sophie), optional: Jordan (procurement lead) if needed
Context / goal: triage pending procurement approvals that materially affect monthly cashflow and MRR-affecting vendor commitments for next 90 days. Walk through ask list, clarify approval paths, and lock decisions for any >$75k annual commitments.

Top priorities to surface quickly:
- Vendor renewals in next 45 days: SAML SSO provider (AuthWave) renewal due 4/20 - $84,000/yr (renewal vs multi-year discount). Needs VP sign-off if >$80k? currently flagged for CFO since borderline.
- Observability seats (TelemetryCo) add 150 seats for new infra team ramp: one-time commit $42k + $9k/yr support. Below CFO threshold but requires procurement notice.
- Dedicated capacity contract (GPU pool) commit increase: proposal from infra to add 2 dedicated nodes q3 start. Estimated incremental committed spend ~$120k/yr (capex vs opex discussion). Definitely requires exec approval and change to dedicated capacity contract.
- Enterprise LLM model licensing pilot (VendorX): pilot proposed $60k for 6 months (consumable credits). Check budget code and whether this counts as R&D / product spend.

Quick numbers (back-of-envelope) for talk-through:
- Current monthly net burn estimate (Feb actual + planned): $2,200,000/month.
- Headcount-driven run for next quarter (hiring runway add): +$220k/month incremental payroll.
- If we approve Dedicated capacity + AuthWave renewal, annualized incremental committed spend ~ $204k -> ~ $17k/month impact.
- Cash runway sensitivity: each $100k annual commitment ~ $8.3k/mo; include in scenario table later.

Questions / decisions I need from Sam:
1) Approval threshold confirmation: CFO approves up to $100k/yr or $100k total? (current policy doc ambiguous)
2) Preferred classification: treat Dedicated capacity increase as OPEX (service) vs CAPEX — impacts monthly P&L and free cash. Need quick guidance for forecasting.
3) Any risk tolerance for multi-year vendor discounts that require prepay? Current treasury prefers 12-month prepay only if >10% discount.
4) Contract sign-off flow: if VP-product signs, does procurement still need legal review for >$50k?

Draft agenda (10–15 min):
- 0–3m: Quick status on runway and hiring cadence (highlight 2 immediate commit asks)
- 3–10m: Walk vendor asks (AuthWave, Dedicated capacity, VendorX pilot) with recommended decision for each
- 10–15m: Action items and next steps (owners + due dates)

Recommended decisions (my call notes) to pitch: 
- AuthWave: accept 2-year term for 5% discount if treasury ok with 12-month prepay clause; CFO sign-off required.
- Dedicated capacity: approve increase but require a 90-day canary with opt-out clause; route through infra and legal, CFO to sign.
- VendorX pilot: approve under R&D bucket, cap at $60k for pilot, product to report usage weekly.

Risks / flags to raise:
- Several asks clustered in same month -> cashflow smoothing needed; propose shifting non-critical renewals to next fiscal quarter if possible.
- Prepay commitments reduce short-term cash runway; double-check cash forecast for May/June.
- Procurement lead times: AuthWave requires 30 business days for SAML transition (if changing plan). If we delay decision beyond 3/24, likely hit service gap.

Open items for follow-up (action log):
- [Sophie] Confirm approval thresholds with legal & procurement policy (due 2026-03-15) -> quick ping Legal: legal@redwood.ai and procurement slack #procurement.
- [Jordan] Get final pricing breakdown from AuthWave (is 5% for 2-yr true or marketing) (due 2026-03-13)
- [Avery] Confirm telemetry seat pricing floor and discount triggers for >200 seats (due 2026-03-14)
- [Infra lead, cc Jordan] Provide detailed expected throughput changes if Dedicated capacity added (affects cost-per-inference) (due 2026-03-20)
- [Sophie] Update cashflow model with two scenarios (approve all vs defer Dedicated) and push to Sam before EOD 3/12.

Notes-to-self (scratch style):
- If Sam asks about runway impact, show the simple scenario table: base burn, +hiring, +commits (AuthWave, Dedicated), sensitivity +/- 10% revenue. Keep slides to 1 table.
- Keep procurement policy link handy: confluence link in linked_artifacts.
- If CFO pushes to defer, prepare justification for Dedicated (risk to latency and product SLOs) — get infra metrics showing current utilization >75% at peak.

Follow-up email draft bullets after meeting:
- Summarize approvals (list each vendor + decision + owner + due date)
- Attach updated cashflow scenarios and highlight any prepay that needs treasury sign-off
- Ask legal to prep contract redlines for AuthWave and Dedicated capacity if approved

Everything below is raw scratch:
- Consider negotiating an easier opt-out on Dedicated capacity in first 6 months (service-level break clause).
- Could we convert a portion of GPU committed spend into on-demand bursts for q3 to reduce commit? Ask infra for cost comparison.
- Note: VendorX pilot has a clause about sublicensing that legal flagged in earlier review - check FIN-412 ticket.

End of scratchpad.
